name: Tax invoice under the CGST Rules
definition: A tax invoice is the document a registered person issues for a taxable supply. Rule 46 fixes what it must contain: eighteen particulars, (a) to (r), some unconditional and some triggered by the facts of the supply.
why_it_exists: It is the primary evidence of a taxable supply and the document input tax credit is claimed on. Rule 46 turns 'what does an invoice say' from a matter of practice into a closed list, which is exactly what a field-extraction contract needs.
inputs: an image or file of a supplier document
the value of the taxable supply
whether the invoice was prepared under rule 48(4)
outputs: the set of rule 46 particulars found on the document
the set of mandatory particulars that are absent
preconditions: the document is issued by a registered person for a taxable supply
rule 54 does not displace the particulars for this class of supplier
exceptions: rule 54 displaces or relaxes particulars for Input Service Distributors, insurers, banking companies, financial institutions, goods transport agencies, passenger transport and multiplex cinema tickets
rule 46A permits a single invoice-cum-bill of supply where taxable and exempt supplies go to an unregistered person
an electronic invoice under the Information Technology Act, 2000 needs no signature
common_mistakes: treating clause (e) and clause (f) as one rule — they carry different triggers, fifty thousand rupees or more versus less than fifty thousand rupees on request
demanding place of supply on every invoice — clause (n) applies only to inter-State supplies
demanding quantity on a services invoice — clause (i) is 'in case of goods'
treating a missing signature as always defective — it is not required on a compliant electronic invoice
reading rule 46 as if it stood alone — it opens 'Subject to rule 54'
legal_references: UNKNOWN — section 31 of the CGST Act, which rule 46 implements, is a different document and was not read for this record
icai_references: NOT APPLICABLE — the contents of a tax invoice are fixed by the CGST Rules, not by an accounting standard
gst_references: UNKNOWN — source is the Rules as at 01-01-2022; later amendments not held locally
evidence_required: the taxable value of the supply
confidence_factors: weak when the supplier's GSTIN is illegible — clause (a) cannot be confirmed
weak when the recipient's registration status is unknown — clauses (d), (e) and (f) cannot be selected between
weak when the document may fall under rule 54, because the required particulars then change
validation_checks: the serial number is at most sixteen characters
clause (i) is present when the supply is of goods
clause (n) is present when the supply is inter-State
clause (o) is present when the delivery address differs from the place of supply
clause (r) is present when the invoice was prepared under rule 48(4)
examples: a registered supplier's invoice to a registered buyer carrying GSTIN of both, serial number, date, HSN, description, quantity, taxable value, rate and amount of CGST and SGST, reverse-charge flag and a signature — rule 46 satisfied
counterexamples: a document with no serial number — clause (b) fails, and rule 46 is not satisfied however complete the rest is
a document issued by a person notified under rule 48(4) but prepared outside that manner — rule 48(5) says it is not an invoice at all

evidence.quote: 46. Tax invoice.-Subject to rule 54, a tax invoice referred to in section 31 shall be issued by the registered person containing the following particulars, namely,-
name, address and Goods and Services Tax Identification Number of the supplier;
signature or digital signature of the supplier or his authorised representative:
the number of digits of Harmonised System of Nomenclature code for goods or services that a class of registered persons shall be required to mention; or
evidence.extraction_note: The proviso lets the Board vary the HSN digit requirement by notification. No such notification is held locally, so the number of digits required is UNKNOWN.
